label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents a group of 128 respondents characterized by notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. Their scores across all three psychological measures fall well below clinical thresholds, suggesting generally positive mental health and emotional well-being. They report minimal psychological distress across all assessed domains.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.81), indicating strong social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.31), well below clinical concern thresholds
Near-negligible anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.04), suggesting very low worry or tension
Moderate and controlled screen/internet usage (1–3 hours daily)
Higher educational attainment suggesting structured daily routines and goal orientation

label: High-Distress Heavy-Use Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily on social media and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Across all three distress dimensions—loneliness (UCLA-8 mean 1.62), depression (PHQ-9 mean 1.65), and anxiety (GAD-7 mean 2.06)—scores are notably high, with anxiety being the most pronounced. The combination of extended screen time and graduate-level education suggests a population that may be digitally immersed for both professional and personal reasons, yet experiencing significant psychological burden.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily social media use
behavior_markers: Extended daily social media use exceeding 5 hours
Elevated loneliness scores indicating perceived social isolation despite digital connectivity
Moderate-to-high depressive symptomatology as measured by PHQ-9
Highest anxiety levels among profiles, with GAD-7 mean above 2.0
Potential disconnect between high educational attainment and emotional well-being
tone: Clinically concerned and empathetic; this profile reflects a population under substantial psychological strain across multiple dimensions of mental health
